Harbor notebook

Harbor lights were still on when we reached the breakwater. The last lighthouse keeper was watching the tide.

Inside the sheltered cove the morning was quiet enough to hear the small wooden boats settle against the pier.

Nested inside the same inlet, a stone bench offered a place to sit and draw the line of the coast.

Beyond the eastern steps, the path narrowed as the grass climbed toward a stand of windblown pines.

Back in the open, we stopped to note the name of each bird and the position of the sun.
